raw_comment:
Hard to count the lines, but about 2/3 of the time the dollar rose, and 1/3 it declined. While the drop this year was the largest percentage decline since 1986 there is a limit what can be deduced from this. Thanks to all the students who responded.   Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:

    The next graph will be released by Friday, October 3.  The topic will be sonic booms!
    Signing off – Jamie Perrett from Salem, Utah, who doesn’t carry money in his wallet for fear of spending it all, and Tom Rothery from Gilbert, Arizona, who is ready to spend all of his cash on Halloween candy for neighboring kids.

raw_comment:
I noticed that the worth of the the US dollar has dropped dramatically since 1986. The worth has been trending down since the mid 1990s according to this graph, where as many other countries have been trending upward. I wonder why this is. This relates to me because I go out of the country often and this is helpful in understanding the ever changing exchange rates.

    What do you wonder?

Everything is increasing in price and jobs pay aren’t paying more to help with the increase in price. Causing people like my own family and others struggling significantly.
    
    Headline: “America is everything but great again”

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
    
    Looking at this graph, my attention is brought to the red line growing downwards.  I can also see that the red line is labeled with the year 2025 and a -10.7% next to it. I can infer that this graph is showing that from 1986-2025 the value of a dollar has decreased by 10.7% I notice that 2025 is not the lowest line shown on the graph, but it is very low compared to the majority of the other lines.
    
    What do you wonder?
    
    This makes me wonder what factors contribute to determining the worth of a dollar? It also makes me wonder what year was the lowest value and what was the highest? Based on my knowledge, I would think the less value a dollar is bad, but I wonder if the value of a dollar can have a good or bad effect on the economy? 
    
    How does this relate to you and your community?
    
    This relates to my community because I have been hearing a lot about inflation in local shops. While it doesn't effect me directly yet, I have heard that the price of cars, houses, groceries, and interest rates have increased greatly. 
    
    A catchy headline could be "How Much is Your Dollar Really Worth?".

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
    Looking at this graph, I notice that through the years, the value of a US dollar has significantly dropped. Each gray line represents a different year aging back to 1986. Some years, the value of a dollar increased, meanwhile in other years, it decreased. It has dropped significantly in only the year 2025, more than most years ever. 
    
    What do you wonder?
    I wonder what caused this significant of a drop. Does it have to do with major inflation? Maybe the tariffs that were imposed. Either way, it is not a good sign. I can guess that the big drops have to do with economic recession. 
    
    How does this relate to you and your community?
    This relates to my community and I because I have noticed that things have been getting far more expensive. Although I live in a town with some pricey stores, even those stores seem to be bumping up their prices to accommodate to the falling economy. It is interesting because when I was younger, things always seemed in a decently affordable price range, but now I am second guessing whether or not to buy things because it seems ridiculous how expensive they are. 
    
    Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea:
    The Dollar's Journey: Ups, Downs, and All In Between

raw_comment:
Looking at the graph, I notice that the U.S. dollar index in 2025 has dropped much more sharply than in almost every other year since 1986, falling about 10.7% in just the first half of the year. This stands out because most years tend to stay closer to the middle, with smaller increases or decreases. I wonder what exactly caused the dollar to fall so much this year, whether it’s because of inflation, changes in interest rates, or issues with global trade. This relates to me and my community because the value of the dollar impacts the cost of everyday things like food, gas, and electronics, and even affects travel and local businesses that buy or sell overseas. A weaker dollar could make imports more expensive, which consumers might feel at the store, but it could also help some U.S. companies that export goods.
    
    A catchy title for this graph could be: From Strong to Struggling: The Dollar’s 2025 Freefall

raw_comment:
Looking at the graph, I notice that the U.S. dollar index in 2025 has dropped much more sharply than in almost every other year since 1986, falling about 10.7% in just the first half of the year. This stands out because most years tend to stay closer to the middle, with smaller increases or decreases. I wonder what exactly caused the dollar to fall so much this year—whether it’s because of inflation, changes in interest rates, or issues with global trade. This relates to me and my community because the value of the dollar impacts the cost of everyday things like food, gas, and electronics, and even affects travel and local businesses that buy or sell overseas. A weaker dollar could make imports more expensive, which we might feel at the store, but it could also help some U.S. companies that export goods
    
    A catchy title : From Strong to Struggling: The Dollar’s 2025 Freefall

What do you notice?
    - What I notice about this graph is that the US dollar's worth started out about 2% up in January. By February it was already down at -1%. By March it had taken a drastic turn at around -5%. The worth of the dollar continued to go down to close to -10%. At June, the worth of the US dollar ended up decreasing by 10.7%. 
    
    What do you wonder?

    How does this relate to you and your community?
    - This relates to me and my community because me and everyone else uses money and should know how this affects us. 
    
    Is money now worthless? How the worth of the US dollar has changed.

raw_comment:
Observations? : I notice there is one squiggle line that’s highlighted red, which I am made to believe is the focal point of the distribution. The red line’s lowest point is around late April, and starting from mid to late January, the line experienced a trend of exponential decay. 
    Wonders? : The data’s caption indicates that the data is related to the worth of a dollar bill. I wonder why low currencies, like the dollar bill and 5 dollar bill are not as valuable anymore, and what factors contribute to that change. 
    How does this apply to your life? : This graph is relevant to me because I spend money on food and school supplies. It’s fascinating to put money into perspective from modern time to different times in history because it shows how the value of money has declined over time. For example, my sports medicine teacher buys a box of 16 medical tape rolls for $80, but she said it used to cost her about $30. So each tape today is $5, but “back then,” was $1.87. In present day, if she didn’t spend more on tape, she could only afford up to 6 rolls, which is 38% less tape. In the past, a $1.87 could get her single roll, but now, she can’t even afford to purchase one with that same amount. 
    Create a catchy title! : Is your $1 bill useless?

    In this graph, I noticed that our current year 2025 has one of the lowest values measured of the US dollar index at -10.7 percent, which is one of the lowest lines relative to the other years. I also noticed that in 2025, the dollar index has decreased with time so that the index shown in June is significantly less than it was in January at the beginning of the year, seeing that it has a negative slope. 
    2. What do you wonder?
    I wonder if there's a trend throughout the years of the dollar index changing, specifically decreasing, considering the different economic crises that have happened over the years in the US. I also wonder if most of the dollar index values tend to stay constant as the year goes on, or if there's usually some sort of change depending on possibly significant events happening that year.

    "Has the US dollar rendered itself useless in the face of other foreign currencies?"

raw_comment:
What Do You Notice?

raw_comment:
I noticed that the percent change in the U.S. dollar index in the first half of 2025 was pretty close with many other years, until the deep nose dive by the end of June where we hit the lowest number yet. I wonder why the dollar keeps going down if the economy is supposed to be getting better. Is it because of tariffs? or just the amount of money spent by the government and the little given back to the economy due to an old population (high # of retirees)? This relates to me because I live in the US and use the dollar so the more that I keep dollar bills instead of investing money, the more money i'm losing in the long run. 
    
    Title: The Dollar Dips!

raw_comment:
Catchy title:Tariffs are the problem, we need NO taxes on imports.The dollar was the worst in nearly 40 years!!!
    
    I am a strong believer in free trade, I believe tariffs are ruining the dollar. One thing I will point out is that in most years the dollar will start going lower or higher in January then by March we know which way the dollar is going. I am surprised to see in a good amount of years that the value of the dollar huddles around 0% at the end of the first six months. The Chart only goes to -10% and 2025 was at -10.7% so this year went off the chart in a bad way.  In 2025 we can tell by this graph we knew that it was going down in March but I think the lowest in nearly 40 years is a problem with many bad outcomes. The problem with a weaker dollar is the loss of purchasing power of the consumer. I also feel that tariffs drive foreign investors away from the US market, making less growth in the economy which would prevent the US from growing out of the national debt.
    
    I conclusion we need to fix the dollar and get rid of tariffs so the foreign investors can help the US grow out of the National debt.

raw_comment:
Catchy Title: Promised the boost of a century, given the lowest in 50 years: New government policies ironically deliver the lowest dollar value in 50 years
    
    What I notice
    - 2025 is a record low year in all of these years, and has hit the rock bottom after June
    - Other years rebounded such as the other lowest year, which rebounded in may
    - About 40 or 50 lines representing years
    -This graph is maybe about inflation, as the dollar index is more than a tenth less than the some others
    -The dollar value dropped 10.7 percent in only 6 months
    -Ironically, President Trump's campaign focused on increasing the Dollar value and lowering inflation, but the U.S. dollar is at its lowest in 50 years
    -More years have an increase in dollar value rather than a decrease, and many years had a slight decrease of around 1%, but the rebounded to positive change
    
    What I wonder
    - With the steady decline of the U.S. dollar seen in this graph this year, how much lower will the dollar value go?
    -  How much will inflation rise because of this?
    -  How much more can inflation rise before it crashes?
    - How much more can American citizens take, already dealing with massive rises in inflation?

raw_comment:
The first thing I notice is that the US dollar has decreased in value most likely because people use credit cards, debit cards and digital payments more often than actual cash. Another thing that I notice is that the value will keep going down even lower in the future because less and less people are using it. The value may have also become lower because of the tariff on other countries which made items from other countries more expensive. 
    
    I wonder why the value of the US dollar has changed so much since 1986. I also wonder why the value has changed a lot since January of this year. Another thing that I wonder is why at the beginning of each year the amount of the dollars are all squished together but closer to the end they spread out more.
    
    Catchy Title: The downfall of the US dollar is happening, and you're experiencing it!

raw_comment:
1. The value of the dollar is decreasing as time goes on. It may have some periods of increase but those are often short lived. Despite the USA being a world power, the dollar has less worth compared to most other nations.
    
    2. What currency has the highest comparative value? Why is the dollar decreasing so much? What is the dollar missing that is keeping other currencies afloat?
    
    3. With the devaluing of the dollar, prices have increased to make up for the loss in value. As a result, this is pushing my family and my community deeper into poverty to an extreme extent.
    
    4. This is supposedly the "best economy we've ever had"
